source: Hand-written by the Interim team. Read only by scripts/fetch_public.py --build-medlist.
rationale: Build-time rules for turning openFDA drug-label name counts into the small, deterministic con-med name list in docs/CONTRACTS.md section 1.6. This is data-shaping, not clinical logic: the rules engine never reads this file, and nothing here changes a grade or a tier. The core_entries block is the contract's hand-curated list and is always present in the output regardless of what openFDA returns.
size_note: Assembly order is core entries, then EVERY one of the top_generics ranked generics, then brands in generic rank order until max_entries. max_entries must therefore exceed top_generics plus the core list (43, of which about 30 overlap the top generics), otherwise the build fails loudly rather than silently dropping common generics.
min_brand_label_count_note: A label count is repackager volume, not familiarity: Neurontin, Wellbutrin, Cipro, Norvasc and Viagra each sit on 2-3 openFDA labels while 'stay awake' sits on 19. The threshold therefore stays low and junk is removed by the token, blocklist and shape rules below instead.
name_shape_note: The con-med matcher (CONTRACTS 1.7) tries every free-text token of 4+ characters at Levenshtein <= 2, so a 4-letter list entry matches ordinary words ('doxy' <- 'dose', 'body'; 'blip' <- 'slip'; 'urea' <- 'area'). Every entry, generic or brand, needs at least min_name_letters letters in total and every token at least min_token_letters letters (drops 'hi vetic', 'anusol hc', 'm-pap'). The hand-curated core list already satisfies this (shortest: advil, aleve).
max_brand_edit_distance_note: A 'brand' within this Levenshtein distance of its generic is a restatement or a label typo ('losortan' for losartan), not a name worth matching separately. A brand that is a substring of its generic ('doxy' in doxycycline) is a truncation and is dropped too.
keep_verbatim_note: Multi-word names kept exactly as written, checked before any salt stripping (otherwise 'potassium chloride' would collapse to 'potassium').
salt_suffixes_note: Trailing salt / ester / hydrate words removed so 'metformin hydrochloride', 'metformin hcl' and 'levocetirizine dihydrochloride' become the bare base. Only trailing tokens are stripped and at least one token always remains; a name that is nothing but a salt word ('potassium' from POTASSIUM CITRATE, 'calcium' from CALCIUM ACETATE) is dropped unless it is in keep_verbatim.
qualifier_tokens_note: Dropped wherever they appear (along with any token containing a digit or a percent sign).
excluded_terms_note: Whole names that are not medicines a trial participant would report starting or stopping: sunscreen filters, antiseptics, cosmetic bases, electrolytes-as-ingredients, gases, topical counter-irritant rubs, homeopathic preparations.
excluded_tokens_note: Any name containing one of these tokens is dropped (catches the many sunscreen, antiperspirant and antiseptic variants without listing each).
homeopathic_tokens_note: Latin-binomial markers and remedy names typical of homeopathic SPL listings ('kali sulphuricum', 'glonoinum' appeared as 'brands' of potassium and nitroglycerin).
brand_suffix_tokens_note: Dosage-form and line-extension suffixes stripped from the END of a brand name so 'seroquel xr', 'toprol xl', 'ventolin hfa', 'anusol hc', 'lamisil at' and 'cleocin phosphate' merge into the bare brand (salt_suffixes are stripped from brands too).
brand_junk_prefixes_note: Store-brand naming prefixes ('wal-itin', 'wal-dryl' are Walgreens; 'geri-tussin' is Geri-Care).
brand_junk_tokens_note: Store brands, manufacturer names and descriptive 'brand names' from repackagers ('Allergy Relief', 'equate ibuprofen', 'stool softener', 'acid controller', 'bayer aleve', 'stay awake', 'alert', 'soothe') are not brands a participant would say; any brand containing one of these tokens is skipped. The excluded_tokens and homeopathic_tokens lists above apply to brands as well.
brand_blocklist_note: Brand families sold under one name with several DIFFERENT active ingredients. The count-based brand -> generic mapping would pick whichever ingredient has more openFDA labels and present it with confidence 1.0, which is wrong for the other products in the family; these names are therefore never emitted and the participant's verbatim text goes to the coordinator unmatched. Each value records the ingredients that share the name.

brand_blocklist.alka-seltzer: aspirin / sodium bicarbonate / citric acid combinations; Alka-Seltzer Plus cold lines
brand_blocklist.coricidin: chlorpheniramine with acetaminophen or dextromethorphan combinations
brand_blocklist.fleet: sodium phosphates (enema), bisacodyl, glycerin, mineral oil
brand_blocklist.kaopectate: bismuth subsalicylate today; kaolin-pectin and attapulgite historically
brand_blocklist.maalox: aluminum hydroxide / magnesium hydroxide / simethicone combinations
brand_blocklist.midol: acetaminophen / caffeine / pyrilamine and ibuprofen lines
brand_blocklist.mylanta: aluminum hydroxide / magnesium hydroxide / simethicone combinations
brand_blocklist.preparation h: phenylephrine, hydrocortisone, witch hazel, lidocaine lines
